newsitem.title: USA: New York comic sues Monaco's prince.
newsitem.headline: New York comic sues Monaco's prince.

text.p: A U.S. stand-up comic has filed a lawsuit accusing Monaco's Prince Rainier of slapping him during an off-Broadway dinner show.
Timothy Ward claimed in papers filed in Manhattan Supreme Court that the incident occurred on Oct. 29, 1995, during "Pomp, Duck and Circumstance."

Rainier, his daughter Princess Caroline and son Prince Albert attended the show as part of a benefit for the Princess Grace Foundation. Rainier became angry over Ward's jokes about Prince Albert's balding head and eating habits, Ward's attorney Gregory Sioris said on Thursday.

Ward, 32, a comic who doubled as a waiter in the show, alleges in his suit that the widower of Grace Kelly beckoned him to his table, motioned for him to lean over "as though to whisper something" and then "viciously" hit him.

"The show involved a lot of interplay between the dinner guests and the performers who taunt you, tease you and play with you," Ward's attorney said. "You go there knowing you're part of the show. The fact that Rainier whacked my client wasn't proper."
Witnesses said they saw the prince slap the wisecracking waiter, New York's Daily News reported at the time.

Ward claims he suffered back and neck pain and injuries to his nervous system. He is seeking unspecified damages and at least $50,000 in medical expenses and lost wages because he was forced to quit his job in the show, his attorney said.
A spokesman for the Monaco Consulate in New York did not return telephone calls seeking comment.
Also named as a defendant in the lawsuit was the foundation that sponsored the $1,000-a-plate event.
